'''William Gilbert "Gil" Strang''' (born November 27, 1934<ref name="Roselle" />) is an American [[mathematician]] known for his contributions to [[Finite elements|finite element theory]], the [[calculus of variations]], [[wavelet analysis]] and [[linear algebra]]. He has made many contributions to [[mathematics]] education, including publishing mathematics textbooks. Strang was the [[MathWorks]] Professor of Mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="MathWorks" />  He taught [[Linear Algebra]], Computational Science and Engineering, and Learning from Data. His lectures are freely available on MIT OpenCourseWare.

Strang popularized the designation of the [[Rank-nullity theorem|Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra]] as such.<ref name="x792">{{cite arXiv | last=Lu | first=Jun | title=Revisit the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra | date=2021 | eprint=2108.04432 | page=| class=cs.LG }}</ref><ref name="s899">{{cite web | title=Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra |work=Wolfram MathWorld | publisher=Wolfram Research, Inc. | date=May 29, 2014 | url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/FundamentalTheoremofLinearAlgebra.html }}</ref>

==Biography==

Gilbert Strang was born in [[Chicago]] in 1934. His parents William and Mary Catherine Strang migrated to the USA from Scotland.  He and his sister Vivian grew up in Washington DC and Cincinnati, and went to high school at Principia in [[St. Louis]].  

Strang graduated from MIT in 1955 with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in mathematics. He then received a [[Rhodes Scholar|Rhodes Scholarship]] to the [[University of Oxford]], where he received his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] and [[Master of Arts|M.A.]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profile |url=https://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.html?pid=266 |access-date=2026-02-20 |website=math.mit.edu}}</ref> from [[Balliol College, Oxford|Balliol College]] in 1957.

Strang earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] in 1959 as a [[National Science Foundation]] Fellow, under the supervision of  [[Peter Henrici (mathematician)|Peter K. Henrici]]. His dissertation was titled "Difference Methods for [[Boundary value problem|Mixed Boundary Value Problems]]".<ref>{{cite thesis |title=Difference Methods for Mixed Boundary Value Problems |institution=[[University of California, Los Angeles]] |degree=PhD |first=William Gilbert |last=Strang |year=1959 |id={{ProQuest|301900319}}}}</ref>

While at Oxford, Strang met his future wife Jillian Shannon, and they married in 1958. Following his Ph.D. at UCLA, they have lived in Wellesley, Massachusetts for almost all of his 62 years on the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] faculty. The Strangs have three sons David, John, and Robert. They describe themselves as a very close-knit family. He retired on May 15, 2023 after giving his final linear algebra [[lecture]] at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Gil Strang's Final Linear Algebra Lecture | date=May 15, 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lUUte2o2Sn8 |language=en}}</ref>

Strang's teaching has focused on linear algebra which has helped the subject become essential for students of many majors. His video lectures are popular on YouTube and MIT OpenCourseWare. Strang founded Wellesley-Cambridge Press to publish ''Introduction to Linear Algebra'' (now in 6th edition) and ten other books.

Professor Strang's video lectures at MIT are open to everyone. They are watched worldwide (more than 20 million viewers). They include 3 popular courses and the final lecture in 2023<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gilbert Strang's final lecture at MIT |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lUUte2o2Sn8}}</ref>. 

Math 18.06 (Linear Algebra) & Math 18.06SC (with several problems solved by TAs)

Math 18.065 (Linear Algebra and Learning from Data) leading to deep learning and basic AI 

Math 18.085 (Computational Science and Engineering)

==University positions ==
[[File:HadamardConjectureMIT.png|thumb|Strang demonstrates the [[Hadamard conjecture]] at MIT, 2005]]
* PhD student, UCLA (1957–1959) 
* [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]], MIT (1959–1961) 
* [[NATO]] Postdoctoral Fellow, [[Oxford University]] (1961–1962)
* Mathematics faculty, MIT (1962–2023, as a full professor from 1970)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://idss.mit.edu/staff/gilbert-strang/ | title=Gilbert Strang }}</ref>

He has received honorary titles and fellowships from the following institutes:
* [[Sloan Fellows|Alfred P. Sloan Fellow]] (1966–1967)
*Honorary Professor, [[Xi'an Jiaotong University]], China (1980)
*Honorary Fellow, [[Balliol College]], [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]] (1999)
*Honorary Member, [[Irish Mathematical Society]] (2002)
*Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (2009) 
* [[Honorary degree|Doctor Honoris Causa]], University of Toulouse (2010)
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2012)<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref>
* Doctor Honoris Causa, Aalborg University (2013)
